title.rendered: Team VERTU aims to end on a high at Brands Hatch

excerpt.rendered: Team VERTU will hope to bring the curtain down on...

content.rendered:
Team VERTU will hope to bring the curtain down on the 2026 Kwik Fit British Touring Car Championship in style this weekend when it heads for Brands Hatch for the season finale, whilst also bidding farewell to a long-standing member of the team.

The EXCELR8-run team makes the trip to the famous Kent circuit for three races around the full Grand Prix layout seeking to wrap up second in the championship standings before turning focus towards trying to reclaim the title in 2027.

Tom Ingram is the best placed of the Team VERTU quartet going into the season finale, with a narrow five-point lead over Dan Cammish in the battle to end the year as runner-up.

Ingram secured his third win of the year last time out at Silverstone and has an astonishing record around the Brands Hatch GP layout, scoring at least one podium in each of the last six seasons.

Maintaining that record this weekend would go some way towards securing the runner-up spot, and would also aid Team VERTU in both the Manufacturers’/Constructors’ and Teams’ Championships.

Experienced teammate Tom Chilton made it four podiums for the season at Silverstone two weeks ago as he seeks to end his BTCC career on a high, with Brands Hatch this weekend marking his final outing in the series.

Chilton debuted on the GP layout in 2002, scoring a podium on his first outing, and has since made more than 550 starts in the series, with 19 wins and 73 podiums to his name, alongside the Independents’ Trophy title in 2010.

Bringing his BTCC career full circle as it ends at the same venue where he debuted, Chilton has his sights firmly fixed on pushing for what would be a second win of the season, having also tasted victory at Knockhill back in August.

Nicolas Hamilton also enjoyed a solid weekend at Silverstone as he continued to extract more pace from his Hyundai following revisions to the special braking system he uses on his car due to his disability.

Hamilton picked up a points finish for the fifth time this season and arrives at the final round sitting third in the Jack Sears Trophy; the award only open to those drivers with no more than one BTCC podium finish to their name.

Further points are the target for Hamilton going into the finale, whilst also seeking to maintain his JST position through the three races this weekend.

As confirmed earlier this week, Ricky Collard rounds out the Team VERTU line-up for the weekend having been drafted into a race seat in place of Osamu Kawashima after the Japanese driver made his series debut at Silverstone.

Qualifying and the qualifying race will run from 13:50 on Saturday and air live on YouTube, with Sunday’s races scheduled for 11:25, 14:35 and 17:15 and all being show on ITV4 and ITVX.

Tom Chilton, #3 Team VERTU Hyundai i30 Fastback N, said: “It’s no secret that I absolutely love Brands Hatch as my home circuit, and the full Grand Prix layout provides a real challenge as a driver as there is no margin for error.

“Going into the weekend on the back of a positive performance at Silverstone, I’m feeling optimistic about my chances and feel confident that we can be in the mix towards the front. The fact that we’ll have full TTB to take into Saturday can only help and hopefully we can secure a strong result there to set us up for Sunday. 

“My BTCC career started on the Brands Hatch GP circuit back in 2002 with a podium finish, so having made the decision to bring my time in the series to an end, it feels appropriate that my final race will be at the same circuit. 

“There are so many fantastic memories from my time in the series, from that debut podium finish in the Vauxhall through to my time with Arena Motorsport in the Honda and Ford, and then the last decade since returning from the World Touring Car Championship.

“Being part of Team VERTU for the last five seasons has been a particular highlight, and I’m hopeful that this weekend, I can bring the curtain down on my BTCC journey with another podium finish - hopefully with a trip to the top step!”

Nicolas Hamilton, #24 Team VERTU Hyundai i30 Fastback N, said: “Silverstone was another positive weekend on the whole as we continued to learn about the changes we made to the car at Croft, and to come away with another points finish was  really pleasing as we move towards the end of the season.

“Brands Hatch GP is a truly iconic circuit and always delivers action on the final weekend of the season, and I don’t expect things to be any different this time around. My goal is to try and maintain the progress that I’ve made as a driver this season to challenge for points, and wrap up a top three finish in the Jack Sears Trophy.”

Tom Ingram, #80 Team VERTU Hyundai i30 Fastback N, said: “Returning to the top step of the podium two weeks ago was a good boost in confidence as we head into the season finale and we head for Brands Hatch in a positive frame of mind - even though there is no longer a championship on the line.

“With the battle for second place being so close with Dan, it’s important that we remain fully focused on the job at hand and maximise every session on track. 

“We know that Brands Hatch GP is a circuit where traditionally we have been strong, and the hope is that we can replicate that form again this weekend to end what has been a challenging season in the best way possible.”

title.rendered: NAPA Racing UK unveils special liveries for Brands Hatch finale

excerpt.rendered: Sutton and Cammish set to sport one-off designs in celebration...

content.rendered:
Sutton and Cammish set to sport one-off designs in celebration of historic title success

NAPA Racing UK has revealed two special liveries for Ash Sutton and Dan Cammish ahead of the 2026 Kwik Fit British Touring Car Championship season finale at Brands Hatch this weekend (10/11 October).

The striking one-off designs commemorate Sutton's record-breaking fifth BTCC Drivers' title and NAPA Racing UK's fifth consecutive Teams' Championship, maintaining the squad's remarkable 100% title-winning record since joining the series in 2022.

Sutton will also swap his familiar #116 for #5 at the Kent circuit, marking his historic achievement after securing the Drivers' crown at Silverstone two weeks ago.

Both liveries take inspiration from NAPA Racing's NASCAR designs, celebrating the brand's continued success in motorsport on both sides of the Atlantic as the team prepares to round off another championship-winning campaign.

title.rendered: Independent Contenders: Mikey Doble

excerpt.rendered: Mikey Doble heads to Brands Hatch (10/11 October) as the...

content.rendered:
Mikey Doble heads to Brands Hatch (10/11 October) as the driver to catch in the Independent Drivers’ Championship, carrying a 25-point advantage into the final weekend of the season.

The LKQ Euro Car Parts with Power Maxed Racing driver leads the standings on 373 points, ahead of Gordon Shedden on 348 and Charles Rainford on 345. Six Independent victories and a further seven top-three finishes have underpinned Doble’s challenge across the opening nine events.

His campaign could hardly have started better. Doble gave the new Audi A3 Saloon a victory on its BTCC debut in the opening race at Donington Park, climbing through the order to take his second career win and briefly lead the overall Drivers’ Championship for the first time. A podium at Brands Hatch followed as the #88 quickly established itself among the regular front-runners.

That early form also translated into a championship lead. By the summer break, Doble sat five points clear at the top of the Independent standings, with consistency keeping him ahead as the battle developed around him. A more difficult Donington Park GP weekend followed after an electrical issue hampered his Saturday, but he remained firmly in contention heading into the closing stages.

Croft then provided one of the biggest moments of his season. After another mechanical issue in the Race to Pole, Doble worked his way into position for the reverse-grid finale before converting pole into a lights-to-flag victory, his second outright success of 2026 and third BTCC win overall. The result left him 33 points clear in the Independent Drivers’ Championship with two events remaining.

Doble carried that momentum into Silverstone, where he claimed pole position and his maiden Race to Pole victory before adding an outright podium on Sunday. The points ensured he would arrive at Brands Hatch still holding a sizeable advantage at the top of the table.

Now, after leading the championship through much of the campaign, Doble has one final weekend to turn that position into a first Independent Drivers’ title.

With 25 points in hand over Shedden, the championship is Doble’s to defend at Brands Hatch.

Independent Drivers’ Championship: 1st – 373 points
Independent Wins: 6
Independent Top-Three Finishes: 13
Overall Drivers’ Championship: 9th – 240 points

title.rendered: Independent Contenders: Gordon Shedden

excerpt.rendered: Gordon Shedden arrives at Brands Hatch (10/11 October) with another...

content.rendered:
Gordon Shedden arrives at Brands Hatch (10/11 October) with another championship still within reach, as the three-time BTCC Champion targets the Independent Drivers’ crown in his first season with Laser Tools Racing with MB Motorsport.

Second in the standings on 348 points, Shedden trails Mikey Doble (LKQ Euro Car Parts with Power Maxed Racing) by 25, with Charles Rainford (WSR) just three points behind. Five Independent wins and a further eight top-three finishes have kept the #52 Toyota firmly in the mix across the campaign.

Shedden's title bid started strongly at Donington Park, where an Independent victory was backed up by an outright podium on debut with his new team. Snetterton then provided one of the defining weekends of his season, with Shedden topping the Independent order in both Race 2 and Race 3, the latter also bringing a 54th career BTCC victory.

Oulton Park proved more difficult heading into the summer break, but Shedden responded during the second half of the year. He returned to the outright podium at Donington Park GP and added another Independent win, before continuing to collect valuable points at Croft.

Silverstone then gave his challenge another boost. From 12th on the grid in a wet Race 3, Shedden climbed to fourth overall and second among the Independent runners to keep the pressure on Doble heading into the finale.

Brands Hatch now provides the final opportunity. With 25 points to make up and everything still to play for, Shedden remains right in contention for a fourth major BTCC title.

Stats

Independent Drivers’ Championship: 2nd – 348 points
Independent Wins: 5
Independent Top-Three Finishes: 13
Overall Drivers’ Championship: 8th – 241 points

title.rendered: Louise Goodman calls time on glittering 30-year ITV career

excerpt.rendered: After three decades at the forefront of British motorsport, much-loved...

content.rendered:
After three decades at the forefront of British motorsport, much-loved presenter Louise Goodman has announced she will be stepping down from her role at ITV.

From the intensity of Formula 1 to the unmistakable drama of the British Touring Car Championship, Goodman has been a brilliant and trusted presence on ITV screens since 1997 – an incredible body of work spanning 30 fantastic years.

Louise’s major broadcasting breakthrough began when ITV secured the UK television rights to Formula 1. Already hugely respected within the paddock following senior communications roles with Leyton House and Jordan Grand Prix, Goodman brought genuine insider knowledge to the channel’s ambitious new coverage.

She became one of ITV’s roving pit-lane reporters, working alongside some of the most recognisable names in sports broadcasting, including Murray Walker, Martin Brundle, Jim Rosenthal, James Allen, Ted Kravitz and Steve Rider.

Across 12 seasons, Goodman reported from the heart of the Formula 1 paddock, covering an era defined by the likes of Michael Schumacher, Mika Häkkinen, Fernando Alonso and of course Lewis Hamilton’s sensational emergence. Her final race with ITV’s original F1 team was the unforgettable 2008 Brazilian Grand Prix, when Hamilton secured his first World Championship on the last corner of the last lap.

Goodman’s impact extended far beyond the questions she asked. She helped break down barriers for women in a traditionally male-dominated field, paving the way for future generations and inspiring many along the way.

While Formula 1 introduced Goodman to a vast national and global audience, it was the British Touring Car Championship that would become the defining and most enduring chapter of her career.

For almost two decades, Goodman has occupied the very centre of the BTCC paddock. Whether reporting live from a rain-soaked grid, capturing the immediate emotion of a first victory or calmly unpicking the aftermath of a controversial collision, Louise has always combined her undoubted talent and professionalism with an instinctive ability to put people at ease.

Alongside the ITV Sport team, Goodman played an integral role in turning the championship’s coverage into a familiar Sunday sporting institution. Louise’s qualities made her one of the finest pit-lane reporters of her generation and one of the most popular figures ever to work in the British Touring Car Championship. 

Everyone across the BTCC, ITV Sport and the wider motorsport community extends their heartfelt thanks to Louise and wishes her every happiness for the future.

Louise Goodman said: “I've decided to step down from ITV Sport's team covering the British Touring Car Championship. It brings an end to an amazing chapter with ITV, which started almost exactly 30 years ago when they took a punt on a total novice and offered me a pit lane reporter role with their brand new F1 team. Since 2007, I have found a very happy, welcoming home in the BTCC paddock and I am going to deeply miss my brilliant, tight-knit immediate team, the wider ITV family, and the countless wonderful people who make up the BTCC and all the support paddocks. 

“To everyone who has been a part of this ride - from F1 to touring cars, on screen, off screen, watching at home or just shouting at your telly when I call someone by the wrong name – thank you. Thank you for the fun, the friendships and most of all the fabulous racing. What a way to earn my pennies all these years. It's been nothing short of amazing.”

title.rendered: Ricky Collard returns to Team VERTU line-up for BTCC finale

excerpt.rendered: Team VERTU can today confirm that Ricky Collard will form...

content.rendered:
Team VERTU can today confirm that Ricky Collard will form part of its driver line-up for the final rounds of the Kwik Fit British Touring Car Championship this weekend at Brands Hatch.

Collard will return to the wheel of the #11 Hyundai i30 Fastback N for the three races around the iconic Grand Prix layout in place of Japanese driver Osamu Kawashima, who was due to contest the event as part of a two-round deal he agreed with the EXCELR8-run team back in June, at which point Ricky was only confirmed until the mid-point of the season. 

Kawashima made his debut in the series at Silverstone last time out, realising his dream of competing in Britain’s premier racing series a decade after his first opportunity to get behind the wheel of a touring car.

While tests prior to Silverstone were successful in demonstrating the necessary performance, it was evident following the race meeting at Silverstone that Kawashima would benefit from additional time in the car to fully realise his potential.

As a result, and given the unique challenges of the Brands Hatch GP layout, the decision has been taken to instead focus on providing Kawashima with additional track time away from the pressures of a race weekend.

As a result, Collard will step up from the role of reserve driver to fill the seat for the season finale as he seeks to end what has been his best BTCC season to date on a high.

Collard originally signed an eleventh-hour deal with the team to compete in the opening five meetings of the season, with the 30-year-old having the option to extend to the full season or until the Croft meeting - with the door open for Kawashima to race in the final two events when Collard chose the latter option.

Despite no pre-season testing, Ricky bagged seven podium finishes at the wheel of the Hyundai and has scored more points this season than in any of his previous BTCC campaigns.

Even after sitting out the Silverstone meeting, Ricky will arrive at Brands Hatch sitting tenth in the standings, and with the opportunity to challenge for the top six around a circuit that was the scene of one of the highlights of his career back in 2024 when he wrapped up the British GT title alongside his father Rob.

Ricky Collard said: “Silverstone was a situation where emotions were running high and things were said in the heat of the moment, but the focus now is on looking ahead to the finale and ending the season on a high.

“I’m grateful to have the chance to get back behind the wheel of the Hyundai this weekend, especially around such an iconic circuit as Brands Hatch GP, and hopefully we can have another strong weekend and build on the results we have gained already this season.

“Seven podiums has been a fantastic return and the only thing missing to complete the set is to make it onto the top step. If we could do that, it would be an amazing way to end the year, not least as I am working with the team to try and make a return to the seat possible for 2027.”

title.rendered: Where to Watch: Brands Hatch GP

excerpt.rendered: The 2026 Kwik Fit British Touring Car Championship heads to...

content.rendered:
The 2026 Kwik Fit British Touring Car Championship heads to Brands Hatch this weekend (10/11 October) for the final event of the year, with championship battles still to be decided.

Following a record-breaking weekend at Silverstone, the BTCC heads to Kent with Ash Sutton holding an unassailable lead as the 2026 campaign enters its final event.

The weekend gets underway with Free Practice, then we go straight into qualifying. Two groups of 15-minute sessions, split according to the finishing order from Free Practice between odd and even finishing positions. The group with the fastest time will take the odd-numbered grid spots for the Qualifying Race. 15 minutes after qualifying, the pit lane opens ahead of the ‘Race for Pole’. A 10-lap race will then take place with half points awarded, as the result forms the grid for the first of the traditional trio of races on Sunday.

Last time out, the 2026 grid headed to Northamptonshire for the ninth race weekend of the championship. After another action-packed Saturday, culminating in the all-new ‘Race to Pole’, Mikey Doble would start Sunday from the front before teammate Aiden Moffat took victory in Race 1. Ash Sutton then secured a record-breaking fifth Drivers’ title with victory in Race 2, before Tom Ingram came through to win the rain-affected final contest. Sutton’s triumph also helped NAPA Racing UK secure the Teams’ Championship, while Alliance Racing/Ford wrapped up the Manufacturers’/Constructors’ crown and Dexter Patterson secured the Jack Sears Trophy.

This weekend’s race day action will feature on the home of the BTCC, ITV4, from 1030 on Sunday (11 October), while the ITV YouTube page will host the Qualifying Race and Qualifying on Saturday (10 October) from 1350.

As in 2025, each race day of the season – including all support series’ races – will be streamed LIVE around the globe on the BTCC YouTube channel, with the exception of the UK and North America, which have existing broadcast arrangements.

The BTCC will be aired LIVE in North America (US and Canada), continuing the multi-year agreement with the RACER Network, streaming live and on demand as part of a long-term agreement with the championship.

All 30 races are scheduled to air on the main RACER channel, whilst support series’ and extended BTCC highlights will be available to watch via the RACER+ App, the network’s premium motorsports streaming platform. Race 1 will begin at 06:25 Eastern Time (ET), with Race 2 following at 09:35 ET and Race 3 closing out the day’s racing at 12:15 ET.

title.rendered: Scott Dennis

excerpt.rendered: The British Touring Car Championship is saddened to learn of...

content.rendered:
The British Touring Car Championship is saddened to learn of the passing of Scott Dennis, the former Motorsport Manager of SEAT UK.

Scott played a pivotal role in bringing the Spanish marque into the BTCC in 2004, overseeing a hugely successful five-year programme that quickly established SEAT as one of the championship’s leading manufacturers. With drivers including Jason Plato, Rob Huff, James Thompson and Darren Turner, SEAT Sport UK claimed numerous race victories, the Manufacturers’ Championship in 2006 and the Teams’ title in 2007.

Scott’s enthusiasm, professionalism and unmistakable passion for motorsport made him a popular and respected figure throughout the paddock.

The thoughts and sincere condolences of everyone connected with the BTCC are with Scott’s family, friends and former colleagues at this very sad time.

title.rendered: Independent Contenders: Charles Rainford

excerpt.rendered: Charles Rainford heads to Brands Hatch (10/11 October) with a...

content.rendered:
Charles Rainford heads to Brands Hatch (10/11 October) with a maiden Independent Drivers’ Championship still within reach following an impressive second season in the BTCC.

The WSR driver sits third in the standings on 345 points, 28 behind championship leader Mikey Doble and just three adrift of Gordon Shedden. Four Independent victories, six second-place finishes and one third have kept the #99 firmly in contention heading into the final weekend of the campaign.

Rainford has also enjoyed a strong trajectory with his best BTCC season in year two. An opening-event podium at Donington Park was followed by a standout weekend at Snetterton, where he won the Race to Pole before converting pole position into victory in Race 1. He then made it back-to-back winning weekends by charging to the front in the Oulton Park finale.

A tougher spell followed during the second half of the campaign, but Rainford has built momentum again as the season has reached its closing stages. Fifth overall at Croft brought his third Independent victory of the year before another strong showing at Silverstone, where he charged to third in Race 2 to secure his fourth outright podium of 2026 and another maximum score in the Independent Drivers’ Championship.

Now the battle moves to Brands Hatch, a venue already responsible for some of Rainford’s biggest BTCC moments. He claimed his maiden victory on the Indy Circuit in 2025 and returns to the Grand Prix layout as its current qualifying lap record holder.

With one weekend remaining, 28 points is the deficit to Doble. Rainford remains firmly in the fight.

Stats

Independent Drivers’ Championship: 3rd – 345 points
Independent Wins: 4
Independent Podiums: 11
Overall Drivers’ Championship: 7th – 247 points

title.rendered: BTCC battles go down to the wire at Brands Hatch

excerpt.rendered: Independent titles and fight for second set to be decided...

content.rendered:
Independent titles and fight for second set to be decided at season finale

The 2026 Kwik Fit British Touring Car Championship heads to Brands Hatch this weekend (10/11 October), with the legendary Grand Prix Circuit hosting Rounds 28, 29 and 30 as another memorable campaign reaches its conclusion.

Aiden Moffat (LKQ Euro Car Parts with Power Maxed Racing – Audi), Ash Sutton (NAPA Racing UK – Ford) and Tom Ingram (Team VERTU – Hyundai) shared the victories last time out at Silverstone, with Sutton’s success in the second contest securing a record-breaking fifth BTCC Drivers’ title.

Alliance Racing/Ford and NAPA Racing UK also wrapped up the Manufacturers’/Constructors’ and Teams’ Championships respectively at the Northamptonshire venue, while Dexter Patterson (Steel Seal with Power Maxed Racing – Audi) secured the Jack Sears Trophy.

There remains plenty to be decided, however, with just five points separating Ingram and Dan Cammish (NAPA Racing UK – Ford) in the fight for second in the Drivers’ standings, while both Independent championships remain very much up for grabs.

All to play for

Reigning champion Ingram heads into the season finale sitting second in the Drivers’ standings on 336 points, just five clear of Cammish following a Silverstone weekend in which the Team VERTU star overturned an eight-point deficit to his rival.

Brands Hatch provides a fitting location for their latest battle, with both drivers having stood on the top step around the Grand Prix Circuit just 12 months ago. Cammish claimed the opening contest of the 2025 season finale before Ingram took victory in Race 2, a result that secured the latter his second BTCC Drivers’ crown. Josh Cook (Speedworks Corolla Racing – Toyota) then completed the weekend with victory in the final race of the year.

Ingram has already enjoyed success at Brands Hatch this season too, taking his first victory of the campaign around the shorter Indy layout back in May, while Sutton and Árón Taylor-Smith (Laser Tools Racing with MB Motorsport – Toyota) also took a win apiece.

The Independent Drivers’ Championship is also finely balanced, although Mikey Doble (LKQ Euro Car Parts with Power Maxed Racing – Audi) remains the man to beat. Doble takes a 25-point advantage over Gordon Shedden (Laser Tools Racing with MB Motorsport – Toyota) into the weekend, having strengthened his position with ‘Race to Pole’ honours and a podium finish at Silverstone.

Charles Rainford (WSR – BMW) sits just three points further back on 345, while Moffat and Daryl De Leon (WSR – BMW) remain firmly in contention on 332 and 330 points respectively. Five drivers therefore arrive at the finale covered by just 43 points.

There is a similarly close fight in the Independent Teams’ Championship, where LKQ Euro Car Parts with Power Maxed Racing leads the way. Laser Tools Racing with MB Motorsport sits 33 points behind, with WSR just a single point further back, ensuring all three squads remain in contention heading into the final event.

At 2.43 miles and ten corners, the Brands Hatch Grand Prix Circuit has regularly provided the setting for pivotal moments in the closing stages of the championship. Rainford holds the current Qualifying benchmark following his 1m28.919s effort in 2025, while Ingram’s 1m29.596s lap from the same year remains the race record.

With Sutton ready to celebrate an unprecedented fifth title and several other battles still to be settled, three final races around one of British motorsport’s most iconic circuits will bring the curtain down on the 2026 season.

TV, Timetables and Tickets

Complementing the tin top racing will be another packed support programme, with the Porsche Carrera Cup Great Britain, Porsche Sprint Challenge Great Britain, Wera Tools F4 British Championship certified by FIA, MINI CHALLENGE and the Caterham Seven Championship UK all in action across the weekend.

Saturday's qualifying sessions and 'Race to Pole' will be streamed live via ITV Sport's YouTube Channel from 1350, with the Qualifying Race getting underway at 1450. ITV4 and ITVX then take over on Sunday from 1030 for more than seven-and-a-half hours of live coverage.

Continuing the championship's expanded global coverage, Sunday's action will also be streamed live via the BTCC YouTube Channel outside the UK and North America, while fans in the United States and Canada can follow the action on the RACER Network. The three BTCC races are scheduled for 1125, 1435 and 1715 (BST).

There's no place like being there, of course, and fans can purchase tickets online in advance or throughout the weekend – visit here for more details.

title.rendered: Speedworks Motorsport targets PM Junior Championship for 2027

excerpt.rendered: Speedworks Motorsport Rising Stars has announced its intention to enter...

content.rendered:
Speedworks Motorsport Rising Stars has announced its intention to enter the PM Junior Championship in 2027.

 

The Rising Stars programme was created by Speedworks with one clear objective: to identify, develop and prepare the next generation of young drivers for a future in the British Touring Car Championship and GT racing.

The arrival of the PM Junior Championship on the BTCC package provides Speedworks Motorsport with an opportunity to take that philosophy another step forward. The purpose-built car will race on the same weekends as the BTCC, within a development environment that connects young drivers directly with a front-running professional race team.

The programme is structured around three key areas:

 

DEVELOP

Coaching, data, simulator, fitness, media, racecraft and career development.

RACE

The opportunity to compete on the biggest stage in British motorsport as part of the BTCC package.

PROGRESS

A genuine pathway towards the next stage of a driver’s career in the BTCC, GT racing and professional motorsport.

 

More than just a junior race programme, Speedworks Motorsport’s initiative is designed to develop the complete racing driver – on the track, off the track and in preparation for what comes next.

 

Drivers interested in being part of the next chapter, exploring opportunities or finding out more about the Rising Stars PM Junior Championship programme should contact danny@speedworksmotorsport.co.uk.

title.rendered: In Pictures: Ash Sutton's Fifth BTCC Title

excerpt.rendered: Ash Sutton wrote his name into the history books at...

content.rendered:
Ash Sutton wrote his name into the history books at Silverstone last weekend, becoming the first driver to win the British Touring Car Championship Drivers’ title on five occasions.

The NAPA Racing UK star sealed the record-breaking crown in fitting fashion, charging from 12th on the grid to victory in Round 26 and establishing an unassailable advantage at the top of the standings. It marked Sutton’s ninth win of a remarkable 2026 campaign and ensured he moved clear of fellow four-time Champions Andy Rouse and Colin Turkington in the record books.

The celebrations began immediately and continued throughout the remainder of a memorable day at Silverstone, with Sutton later adding another podium in the rain-soaked finale.

Take a look through some of the best images from Sutton’s history-making weekend below.

title.rendered: Speedworks rue missed opportunity as focus turns to finale

excerpt.rendered: Speedworks Corolla Racing left Rounds 25, 26 & 27 of...

content.rendered:
Speedworks Corolla Racing left Rounds 25, 26 & 27 of the 2026 Kwik Fit British Touring Car Championship at Silverstone with plenty of positives but also a sense of unfinished business after a weekend in which the team's early pace promised more than the final results ultimately delivered.

Having shown front-running pace earlier in the day, Josh Cook struggled with the balance of the Corolla in Qualifying as a combination of factors prevented him from reproducing the performance shown during practice. He eventually secured 12th on the grid.

Ryan Bensley, meanwhile, continued his impressive progress by qualifying directly behind his vastly more experienced teammate in 13th – a career-best BTCC qualifying result and another important milestone in his development.

Cook immediately set about recovering lost ground in Saturday's Qualifying Race. A determined drive saw him climb six positions to sixth, putting himself firmly back into contention ahead of Sunday's three championship encounters.

Bensley endured a more combative race, losing several positions after being hustled out of position, but the #7 responded strongly, recovering much of the lost ground and once again demonstrating encouraging race pace.

Cook began Sunday's opening race on the soft tyre and continued his charge towards the front, gaining two further positions to cross the line fourth, with the fastest lap of the race.

Bensley elected to run the medium tyre in the opening encounter. In the thick of a fiercely contested midfield battle throughout, he brought the Corolla home in 16th.

The tyre strategies were reversed for the second race, with Cook switching to the medium compound and Bensley moving onto the faster soft tyre. Cook battled hard as the differing tyre performance played out across the field, eventually taking the chequered flag in tenth.

Bensley's race proved more difficult. Despite showing encouraging underlying speed, a few unforeseen glitches contributed to a disrupted encounter and he eventually finished 19th.

Heavy rain transformed the conditions for the final race of the weekend and presented an entirely different challenge around the high-speed Silverstone National Circuit.

Cook once again moved forward, climbing from tenth to seventh in extremely difficult conditions to complete a weekend in which he had made significant progress from his original qualifying position.

For Bensley, the race represented another important experience in his rapidly developing BTCC career. Facing heavy rain and limited visibility in one of Britain's most competitive championships, he negotiated the conditions to move forward and finish 18th. A career-best qualifying result, strong underlying pace and valuable experience in vastly different conditions represented another significant step forward.

For Speedworks Corolla Racing, attention now switches firmly towards the season finale at Brands Hatch GP in two weeks (10/11 October).

Josh Cook, Driver, Speedworks Corolla Racing: "It's a frustrating one because the car felt really good at the start of the weekend and I genuinely thought we were in for a very strong Silverstone.

"Qualifying didn't go the way we expected and from that point onwards we were playing catch-up, but I think we showed good race pace and managed to keep moving forward.

"Going from 12th to sixth in the qualifying race put us back in the mix and we made another couple of places in the first race on Sunday. The medium tyre made Race Two more difficult, but we still came through it and then gained places again in some pretty challenging conditions in the final race.

"We know there's more performance there. The important thing now is understanding why we couldn't carry the pace from practice into qualifying and making sure we maximise everything at Brands Hatch.

Ryan Bensley, Driver, Speedworks Corolla Racing: "There's loads for me to take away from the weekend. Qualifying 13th was a really positive step and probably the biggest indication yet of the progress we're making. I felt comfortable in the car from practice onwards and the pace was really encouraging, particularly when you look at where we were compared to Josh.

"The races threw pretty much everything at me. There was some really hard racing in the midfield, we ran the medium tyre in Race One, had a few difficulties in Race Two and then Race Three was a complete baptism of fire in the rain!

"But that's exactly the experience I need. Every lap I'm learning more about the car, the championship and how you need to race at this level.

"I feel like I'm getting closer every weekend, and qualifying showed that. There's still plenty to learn, but I'm really looking forward to taking another step at Brands Hatch and ending the season strongly."

The BTCC arrived at Silverstone for the penultimate event of the year, showcasing three spectacular races plus another thrilling Qualifying Race in Northamptonshire. The weekend proved a pivotal chapter in the story of the 2026 campaign.

As the season continues towards its climax, take a listen to the eighth instalment of Tin Top Tuesday powered by Power Maxed, which was aired earlier this week (Tuesday, 29 September).

The two-time winner in 2026 spoke about the evolution of the new Audi, his consistent campaign and growing confidence in the BTCC, as well as his battle for the Independent Drivers’ Championship and his hopes for the final event of the season.

Tim Harvey (1992 BTCC Champion & ITV Broadcaster) was the next guest on the show, reflecting on his love for the sport and the research he puts in to every weekend through being so immersed in the paddock. Harvey discussed the narrative around the 2026 season and his praise for Ash Sutton's record-breaking year.

Alan Hyde also caught up with Aiden Moffat (LKQ Euro Car Parts with Power Maxed Racing), after a season-high at Silverstone as the man, one day after celebrating his 30th birthday, walked away as the top points scorer, speaking to Hyde after days of celebration.

Alan Gow (BTCC Chief Executive) was next on the show, speaking on Ash Sutton's fantastic achievement, clinching his fifth BTCC title at Silverstone, along with the current landscape of the championship and looking ahead at what's to come... Including DR. Paul Trafford's Christmas Dinner.

The 2026 Kwik Fit British Touring Car Championship grid now heads to Brands Hatch (10/11 October) for the final event of the campaign.

title.rendered: Rainford scores sublime Silverstone BTCC podium

excerpt.rendered: WSR’s Charles Rainford produced a charging drive to claim his...

content.rendered:
WSR’s Charles Rainford produced a charging drive to claim his fourth 2026 Kwik Fit British Touring Car Championship podium finish at Silverstone.
 

The Horsham racer and teammate Daryl De Leon tallied four top-10 finishes between them to ensure that WSR head into the final round of the year in contention for the Independents Trophy.


Rainford, sporting a new livery for the remainder of the season, started race day from seventh on the grid and after a feisty performance on the medium tyre, he was able to hold position - setting him up for an even stronger showing in the day's second bout.


Making a strong launch in the BMW 330i M Sport, the #99 worked his way up the order on the soft tyre and after finding a way past De Leon late on, the multiple race winner pushed on to secure third overall and a fourth Independent win. He then closed out his day with points in a wet finale.


De Leon meanwhile showed plenty of front-running pace with two top-five finishes. Celebrating his 100th BTCC race start in the opening exchange, the Anglo-Filipino driver led the contest in the opening exchanges before dropping to fifth late on to others with superior TOCA Turbo Boost.


The reigning Jack Sears Trophy champion opted to run the soft tyre for a second successive time in Race 2 and once again battled for the podium positions, losing out to Rainford late on to secure fourth. He too then fought valiantly to cap off his day with a points finish in the day's final race.


Lewis Gilbert demonstrated pace and potential in his rear-wheel-drive machine. Despite having to endure contact in Race 1 and a slight technical issue in Race 2, he tallied three more finishes, with his best coming in Race 3 as he soared into the points-paying positions in wet conditions.


The 2026 BTCC season concludes around the Brands Hatch Grand Prix circuit (10/11 October).
 

Charles Rainford: “What a day, that’s Silverstone and the penultimate round of the season done; the event where we revealed our incredible new livery. It has been a good day. We said yesterday that we would be in the position to get some trophies and we did just that. Third place and the Independent win in Race Two was brilliant, and we also enjoyed some top ten performances too. All of that has gone towards banking points in the Championship. Let’s give it everything and see you at Brands Hatch.”


Daryl De Leon: “Overall it has been a good day. We set ourselves up for a strong day on Saturday and were able to run towards the sharp end of the grid for a majority of the day - even leading Race Two at one stage. It’s crazy how fast time goes and now we have one more to go. I feel like we can leave this weekend with our heads held high. Although we haven’t got any pots, it has been a strong weekend.”


Lewis Gilbert: “That’s race day finished at Silverstone and it was a bit of an up and down day as things didn’t ideally play out like we hoped. We got caught up in an incident in Race One and then had a slight problem at the start of Race Two. I was glad to make up some positions in Race Three and grab a point. To end the day on a high leaves me pleased and now I’m looking forward to signing off the season on a high at Brands Hatch.”

title.rendered: Pole and podium for Doble at Silverstone

excerpt.rendered: Mikey Doble will head into the final rounds of the...

content.rendered:
Mikey Doble will head into the final rounds of the 2026 Kwik Fit British Touring Car Championship season in the box seat when it comes to the battle for the Independents Drivers’ crown after maintaining his lead in the standings at Silverstone.

The LKQ Euro Car Parts with Power Maxed Racing driver tallied a sublime pole position at the Northamptonshire venue, and then followed it up with a podium finish. Those results helped towards ensuring he takes a 25-point lead into next month’s finale at Brands Hatch.

Arriving at the penultimate event of the campaign off the back of claiming a sublime second win of the year at Croft, the Audi A3 Saloon driver continued his rich vein of form by changing to a maiden Qualifying Race victory on Saturday. 

Three years on from clinching a career-first pole position at Silverstone, the 27-year-old reigned supreme as he and teammate Aiden Moffat secured a front row lockout for Sunday’s opening encounter. 

Doble started the 18-lap sprint from pole position after a superb lap in the earlier qualifying session. And after a brief battle with Daryl De Leon in the opening laps, the Surrey-based racer comfortably charged to glory.

Electing to run the soft tyre in race one, Doble lost the lead to Moffat as the lights went out and was forced to fight tooth and nail to remain at the front as a swarm of other cars threatened to send him tumbling backwards.

Showing his fighting spirit, the former Jack Sears Trophy winner quickly settled into a groove and fought back. Making a number of audacious moves, Doble was back up to second in no time at all and from there, he shadowed Moffat to record a famous one-two for the team.

That would be as good as it would get for Doble on race day though, as the combination of the medium tyre and little to no TOCA Turbo Boost meant that he was easy pickings for rival drivers in race two.

Then in a wet reverse grid finale, the front-wheel-drive ace was unable to utilise his remaining soft-compound tyre, keeping him in the midfield, preventing him from even breaking into the points-paying positions.

Mikey Doble: “It’s certainly been a weekend of two halves. We rolled the car out the truck and the thing was on rails on Saturday. I’d like to think of myself as a bit of a Silverstone specialist so it was nice to do what we did in Qualifying and the Race To Pole.

“I didn’t make the best of starts in race one but we managed to fight back and came oh-so close to getting the lead back off Aiden at the end. I have to offer up my congratulations to him because he drove brilliantly all weekend.

“Then with the slower tyre and no boost, we just fell away in race two. That was to be expected, but what wasn’t was becoming a human pinball as other drivers just decided to fire into the side of me in race three.

“I’d have liked to come away with more in those last two races but importantly we have the lead in the Independents and now we can head to Brands Hatch with a good shot of bringing the title home. It’s my home track and one that I love so let’s give it everything we’ve got.”

The 2026 Kwik Fit British Touring Car Championship campaign concludes in less than two weeks as Rounds 28, 29 & 30 play out around the legendary Brands Hatch Grand Prix circuit (10/11 October).

title.rendered: History Maker

excerpt.rendered: Ash Sutton claims record breaking fifth BTCC title NAPA Racing...

content.rendered:
Ash Sutton claims record breaking fifth BTCC title

NAPA Racing UK's Ash Sutton made motorsport history at Silverstone earlier today (27 September) by winning a record breaking fifth BTCC title.

Running since 1958, the British Touring Car Championship is the third oldest motorsport championship in the world, with only Formula 1 and NASCAR boasting longer histories in the sport.

Andy Rouse and Colin Turkington had been tied four-time winners of the famous old trophy until Sutton joined those tin-top legends back in 2023.

With time and undoubted ability on his side, the 32-year-old has been a true master at work throughout 2026, scoring an incredible nine wins and 19 podiums so far.

Not only is the monster tally of silverware startling in its own right it was also enough to secure this year’s laurels during the penultimate event of the season – a feat not accomplished since Alain Menu 1997’s championship win.

Sutton’s win from 12th on the grid at Silverstone today was one that will live long in the memory, as will the celebrations that followed.

Sutton wasn’t the only story of the day as Aiden Moffat and Tom Ingram also won a race apiece – the former enjoying one of the best weekends of his BTCC career and the latter proving he’ll be ready to try wrestling back the title next season.

Alliance Racing/Ford and NAPA Racing UK moved into an unassailable lead of both the Manufacturers’/Constructors’ and Teams’ standings, whilst Dexter Patterson clinched the Jack Sears Trophy for 2026.

The Independents’ fight will go down to the wire at the season finale with Mikey Doble and his LKQ Euro Car Parts with Power Maxed Racing squad looking to fend off a gaggle of challengers.

So, three unmissable races around the legendary Brands Hatch Grand Prix Circuit will close out the 2026 Kwik Fit British Touring Car Championship in two weeks’ time (10/11 October), but for now it’s all about Ash Sutton – a phenomenal winner of a record five BTCC titles.

Moffat claims maiden 2026 win

LKQ Euro Car Parts with Power Maxed Racing's Moffat stood victorious in the Silverstone opener, becoming the eleventh driver to stand triumphant this year.

The Scotsman started second as teammate Doble led the way in the PMR-run squad's front-row lockout, but it was the #16 who had the better launch, taking the lead into Copse.

Grabbing top spot at the first corner, Moffat would lead until the chequered flag as the Audi A3 Saloon duo took a commanding one-two.

Celebrations continued for the PMR Audi stable, as Dexter Patterson (Steel Seal with Power Maxed Racing) clinched the Jack Sears Trophy to take his first title since joining the BTCC paddock.

Team VERTU's Tom Chilton completed the podium. The #3 Hyundai followed fellow Surrey-racer Doble to the line as both stood on the podium for the second race in a row.

Sutton secures title with 56th career victory

NAPA Racing UK’s Sutton won from 12th on the grid in the second encounter at Silverstone, to take an unassailable lead on his way to an incredible and unprecedented fifth BTCC title.

The #116 started the second race of the day from the sixth row of the grid, ascending to the front of the field by lap nine of the 22-lap race.

Despite only needing a single point to secure the title, that was never going to be the way in which the sensational Sutton wanted to make history.

A flurry of passes took place during his charge through the order with his final move by early leader Daryl De Leon being a wonderful advert for everything that Sutton is about, as he slightly moved to the left before jinking sharply to the right and down the inside of the BMW on the run to Copse.

The Ford Focus Titanium man cruised to the finish, even having time for a burnout across the line, as his NAPA Racing UK squad celebrated wildly.

Behind, Adam Morgan (CPRL – Mercedes) climbed from eighth on the grid to the second step on the podium, with Charles Rainford (WSR – BMW) completing the rostrum positions after starting the race alongside Morgan.

Ingram triumphs in wet Silverstone finale

Team VERTU's Ingram claimed the honours in Round 27 of the 2026 Kwik Fit British Touring Car Championship, standing on the top step of the podium for the first time since Thruxton back in July.

Starting from the front row, Ingram initially dropped back down to fourth. After finding a rhythm in the heavily rain-affected race, the #80 made his way through the field and took the lead from Moffat (LKQ Euro Car Parts with Power Maxed Racing – Audi) at just over half-race distance.

Moffat, starting from pole position and having already taken a win in the day's opening race, reclaimed his lead on lap six after initially falling behind Árón Taylor-Smith (Laser Tools Racing with MB Motorsport – Toyota) and Daniel Rowbottom (CPRL – Mercedes) on the opening tour.

Sutton finished second after a charge from ninth on the grid, whilst Moffat completed the podium.

Fourth on the road went to the Toyota of Laser Tools Racing with MB Motorsport's Gordon Shedden as the Scot gained eight places throughout the wet contest, closing in on Independents Trophy leader Doble (LKQ Euro Car Parts with Power Maxed Racing – Audi) ahead of the Brands Hatch season finale.

Ash Sutton, NAPA Racing UK, said: “I don't think this is going to sink in. Everything has been pretty special today, in every way, and it’s actually been an emotional one. I've been trying to hide it for a lot of the day. There was a phase where I probably could have got the title won in race one, but that wasn't the true Ash style to go and get the fifth. So, I spiced it up a little bit and made sure it went to race two. Like I said, I wanted to do it in the true Ash style, and I hope I have done.

“The fifth feels like the most special. There's a full force of people behind us, so it’s great to reward them. We've done it in such a manner, and it's going down in the history books for many reasons. Of course, the first title was always going to stick with me, but this is above and beyond.

“To have my boys here today has been very special. I promised Sonny when he was born that I'd get him a championship, which we did in 2023. And, ever since Hadley's been born, I've owed him one, so I've just paid that debt, and now we can celebrate!”
